apollo_11.title: Apollo 11: The First Lunar Landing
apollo_11.description: Launch on Saturn V from Kennedy Space Center LC-39A, insert into Low Earth Parking Orbit, perform Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI), execute Lunar Orbit Insertion (LOI), descend to Mare Tranquillitatis with the Lunar Module Eagle, and return safely to Earth splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.

initial_orbit.notes: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) parking orbit used for spacecraft systems checkout prior to TLI.

target_orbit.destination_name: Low Lunar Orbit & Mare Tranquillitatis Surface

flight_phases.description: Saturn V S-IC, S-II, and initial S-IVB burn placing CSM and LM into 185 km parking orbit.
Second S-IVB ignition accelerating the stack to 10.8 km/s onto translunar trajectory.
Service Propulsion System (SPS) retrograde burn behind the Moon to establish lunar orbit.
Descent stage TRW engine throttled to gently lower LM Eagle onto the lunar surface.
Ascent stage ignition launching from the Moon to dock with Columbia in lunar orbit.
Final SPS burn sending Columbia back to Earth for high-speed atmospheric skip reentry.

primary_objectives.title: Execute Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI)
primary_objectives.description: Accelerate spacecraft stack into hyperbolic lunar transfer orbit within burn window.

primary_objectives.title: Perform Lunar Orbit Insertion
primary_objectives.description: Capture into stable low lunar orbit with periapsis near 100 km.

primary_objectives.title: Touchdown at Mare Tranquillitatis
primary_objectives.description: Execute powered descent and safely land LM Eagle with remaining fuel margin.

secondary_objectives.title: Deploy Early Apollo Science Package
secondary_objectives.description: Install seismometer and laser ranging retroreflector on the lunar surface.

secondary_objectives.title: Perform Orbital Rendezvous & Docking
secondary_objectives.description: Ascend from lunar surface and execute radar-guided docking with CSM Columbia.

historical_milestones.event: Lunar Module Eagle touches down: 'Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.'
Columbia command module splashes down in the Pacific Ocean.

voyager_1_2.title: Voyager 1 & 2: Exploration Beyond the Solar System
voyager_1_2.description: Twin robotic spacecraft utilizing a rare planetary alignment of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune to explore the outer solar system, map planetary magnetospheres, and enter interstellar space.

initial_orbit.notes: Short parking orbit before Centaur second burn and Star 37E solid kick burn.

flight_phases.description: Titan IIIE, Centaur D-1T, and Star 37E boost the probe to a heliocentric escape velocity of 15.3 km/s (C3 = 106 km^2/s^2).
Gravitational assist from Jupiter bends trajectory toward Saturn and increases probe velocity by ~16 km/s.
Saturn gravity assist deflects Voyager 1 north out of the ecliptic plane toward interstellar space.
Continuous cruise recording solar wind termination shock and crossing the heliopause into interstellar plasma.

primary_objectives.title: Achieve Interplanetary Escape Velocity
primary_objectives.description: Achieve hyperbolic escape velocity relative to Earth with high characteristic energy.

primary_objectives.title: Execute Jupiter Gravity Assist
primary_objectives.description: Fly within 350,000 km of Jupiter to gain orbital momentum and image the Great Red Spot.

primary_objectives.title: Cross the Heliopause
primary_objectives.description: Detect the boundary where the solar wind gives way to interstellar matter.

secondary_objectives.title: Preserve the Golden Record
secondary_objectives.description: Safeguard humanity's cultural and scientific message into deep space.

historical_milestones.event: Voyager 1 closest approach to Jupiter, discovering active volcanic eruptions on Io.
Voyager 1 crosses the heliopause into interstellar space at 121 AU from the Sun.

hubble_deployment_sts_31.title: Hubble Space Telescope Deployment (STS-31)
hubble_deployment_sts_31.description: Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-31) launches with the Hubble Space Telescope in its payload bay, climbing to an unprecedented Shuttle altitude of 612 km to deploy the optical observatory with the Canadarm.

initial_orbit.notes: Direct insertion high-altitude orbit to minimize residual atmospheric drag on the telescope.

target_orbit.destination_name: High Low Earth Orbit (612 km Circular)

flight_phases.description: 3x RS-25 SSME engines and twin SRBs lift Discovery; dual OMS burns circularize orbit at 612 km.
Payload bay doors open; Remote Manipulator System (Canadarm) grapples and lifts Hubble into deployment position.
Solar array wings unroll; high-gain dish antennas articulate into position.
Canadarm releases Hubble; Discovery performs gentle RCS separation burn to prevent plume contamination.
Discovery executes OMS retrograde de-orbit burn and lands at Edwards Air Force Base Runway 22.

primary_objectives.title: Achieve High LEO Altitude (>600 km)
primary_objectives.description: Deliver Shuttle Discovery and Hubble to record orbit altitude above 600 km.

primary_objectives.title: Execute Canadarm Payload Release
primary_objectives.description: Safely lift, verify solar array unfurl, and release the telescope without physical contact.

secondary_objectives.title: Prevent Mirror Plume Contamination
secondary_objectives.description: Perform separation maneuvers using Low-Z RCS thruster modes to protect optical mirrors.

historical_milestones.event: Hubble Space Telescope successfully released from Canadarm into free flight.
Discovery lands smoothly at Edwards Air Force Base.

jwst_l2_deployment.title: James Webb Space Telescope: Journey to Lagrange Point 2
jwst_l2_deployment.description: Launch on an Ariane 5 ECA from Guiana Space Centre, direct injection onto trans-L2 trajectory, execute complex 29-day deployment sequence (solar array, sunshield, secondary mirror, primary mirror wings), and insert into halo orbit around Sun-Earth L2.
jwst_l2_deployment.launch_site: Guiana Space Centre ELA-3, Kourou, French Guiana

initial_orbit.notes: Direct injection trans-L2 hyperbolic trajectory by Ariane 5 ESC-A upper stage.

target_orbit.destination_name: Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 2 (L2) Halo Orbit (~1.5 Million km from Earth)

flight_phases.description: Ariane 5 Vulcain 2 core and HM7B upper stage insert Webb directly into trans-L2 transfer orbit.
Webb onboard SCAT thrusters fire 12.5 hours after launch to fine-tune trajectory toward L2.
Tensioning of 5-layer Kapton sunshield, deployment of secondary mirror tripod and primary mirror side wings.
Final 5-minute burn inserting observatory into quasi-periodic halo orbit around Sun-Earth L2.

primary_objectives.title: Achieve Trans-L2 Trajectory
primary_objectives.description: Ariane 5 precise injection avoiding any overspeed burn (Webb cannot turn around due to sensitive optics).

primary_objectives.title: Deploy 5-Layer Kapton Sunshield
primary_objectives.description: Fully extend and tension all five sunshield layers to isolate mirror from solar infrared radiation.

primary_objectives.title: L2 Halo Orbit Insertion
primary_objectives.description: Execute MCC-2 burn to enter stable periodic halo orbit around Lagrange Point 2.

secondary_objectives.title: Preserve 20-Year Fuel Lifetime
secondary_objectives.description: Minimize propellant expenditure during MCC maneuvers to exceed nominal 10-year design life.

historical_milestones.event: Ariane 5 liftoff from Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana.
Primary mirror second wing latches into place, completing all major mechanical deployments.
Webb completes MCC-2 burn, safely entering halo orbit around Sun-Earth L2.

curiosity_msl.title: Mars Science Laboratory: Curiosity Rover Landing
curiosity_msl.description: Launch on an Atlas V 541, execute Trans-Mars Injection (TMI) and 254-day interplanetary cruise, perform guided atmospheric entry with hypersonic lifting body, deploy supersonic parachute, ignite Sky Crane Mars Landing Engines, and lower Curiosity onto the floor of Gale Crater.

initial_orbit.notes: Atlas V Centaur parking orbit prior to TMI burn.

target_orbit.destination_name: Mars Surface (Gale Crater / Aeolis Palus, -4.59° S, 137.44° E)

flight_phases.description: Atlas V 541 lifts stack; Centaur upper stage reignites to impart 3.8 km/s TMI burn toward Mars.
Spin-stabilized cruise with 4 Trajectory Correction Maneuvers (TCM) targeting entry corridor.
Guided lifting entry in aeroshell with PICA heatshield dissipating 99% of kinetic energy.
Supersonic disk-gap-band parachute deploys at Mach 1.7; radar altimeter locks onto surface.
Sky Crane ignites 8x throttleable MLE thrusters, lowers Curiosity on tethers, cuts bridles, and flies away.

primary_objectives.title: Execute Trans-Mars Injection (TMI)
primary_objectives.description: Accelerate spacecraft onto hyperbolic Mars intercept trajectory.

primary_objectives.title: Precision Guided Atmospheric Entry
primary_objectives.description: Guide lifting entry to deliver spacecraft inside a tight 20 x 7 km landing ellipse.

primary_objectives.title: Execute Sky Crane Touchdown
primary_objectives.description: Lower rover on 7.5m tethers and achieve soft touchdown (<0.75 m/s) in Gale Crater.

secondary_objectives.title: Evaluate Past Habitability in Gale Crater
secondary_objectives.description: Sample ancient mudstones and test for organic carbon compounds using SAM and CheMin.

historical_milestones.event: Atlas V 541 lifts off from Space Launch Complex 41.
Touchdown in Gale Crater: 'Touchdown confirmed. We're safe on Mars.'
